description.text: We are a biopharmaceutical company focused on delivering novel therapeutics for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (“MASH”), a serious liver disease with high unmet medical need that can lead to cirrhosis, liver failure, liver cancer, need for liver transplantation and premature mortality. MASH was previously known as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (“NASH”). MASH is the leading cause of liver transplantation in women, the second leading cause of all liver transplantation in the United States and the fastest-growing indication for liver transplantation in Europe. Our medication, Rezdiffra (resmetirom), is a once-daily, oral, liver-directed thyroid hormone receptor beta (“THR-β”) agonist designed to target key underlying causes of MASH. In March 2024, Rezdiffra became the first therapy approved by the FDA for patients with MASH and was commercially available in the United States beginning in April 2024. Following receipt of conditional marketing authorization (“CMA”) from the European Commission (“EC”), we launched Rezdiffra in Germany in September 2025. Rezdiffra was the first medication approved by both the FDA and EC for the treatment of adults with noncirrhotic MASH with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis (F2 to F3 fibrosis). We are also evaluating Rezdiffra in patients with compensated MASH cirrhosis (consistent with F4c fibrosis) in our MAESTRO-NASH OUTCOMES trial, that, if successful, could expand the eligible patient population for Rezdiffra.

about.description_short: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: MDGL) is a biopharmaceutical company focused on delivering novel therapeutics for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a liver disease with high unmet medical need. Madrigal's medication, Rezdiffra (resmetirom), is a once-daily, oral, liver-directed THR- agonist designed to target key underlying causes of MASH. Rezdiffra was the first medication approved by both the FDA and European Commission for the treatment of MASH with moderate to advanced fibrosis (F2 to F3). An ongoing Phase 3 outcomes trial is evaluating Rezdiffra for the treatment of compensated MASH cirrhosis (F4c). For more information, visit www.madrigalpharma.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

analysis_md:
# MDGL — Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-18. **In scope** (market cap $10.090B at $449.74, nasdaq_quote_api — under the $40B scope cap).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed. Web-sourced figures are cited as search results.

## What it is
Single-product biopharmaceutical company built on Rezdiffra (resmetirom), a once-daily oral, liver-directed thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist and the first FDA-approved therapy (March 2024) for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with moderate-to-advanced (F2–F3) liver fibrosis. Launched in the U.S. in 2024 and in Germany in September 2025 (per Q2 2026 reporting). Everything else — the oral GLP-1 MGL-2086 (Phase 1 dosing initiated June 2026), ervogastat, and six siRNA programs — is pipeline, acquired or licensed in 2025–26 and unapproved. One product is 100% of revenue.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow -$189,553,000; capex $467,000; SBC $98,130,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: -$288,150,000 = $-12.84/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $-12.84, latest FY OE total $-288.1M, shares diluted 22,434,310).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): -$260,403,000 (financials_history.csv) — same ballpark, same sign.
- OE positive **0 of the last 5** fiscal years. Per-year conservative OE/share (financials_history.csv): FY2023 -$20.09, FY2024 -$25.24, FY2025 -$12.84 — the loss per share is narrowing as revenue scales, and it is still a loss.
- Free cash flow is negative before SBC is even counted: that is the F sub-type (below).

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math), taken because of the STALE_FY flag:**
- OCF: FY -$189,553,000 − prior YTD -$135,943,000 + current YTD -$144,106,000 = **TTM -$197,716,000**
- Capex: FY $467,000 − prior YTD $0 + current YTD $8,102,000 = **TTM $8,569,000**
- SBC: FY $98,130,000 − prior YTD $46,090,000 + current YTD $69,389,000 = **TTM $121,429,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted, ttm.json basis): **29,089,148**
- **TTM OE total -$327,714,000 → base OE/share $-11.27** (key_numbers.md; base_source: ttm_json)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $-20.09/share — it averages in FY2023, a zero-revenue pre-commercial year, so it overstates how bad the current run-rate is; the latest-FY figure is $-12.84/share. Every variant is deeply negative, so the choice of base does not change the tier — it only changes how negative the headline is. The TTM base is the most current and is used.
- Share-count note: the TTM denominator (29,089,148, the current-YTD weighted count in ttm.json) is larger than the engine's latest diluted count (22,434,310 in key_numbers.md); the Q2 2026 release reports a basic-and-diluted weighted count of 29,145,271 including prefunded warrants, convertible preferred and earned PSUs (cited search result). The per-share loss is negative on either denominator.
- Balance sheet (latest FY): **net debt $141.2M** (key_numbers.md; basis LongTermDebtNoncurrent+none — total debt $339,881,000 against cash and equivalents $198,693,000 in financials_history.csv, lease liabilities $7,749,000 in dcf_numbers.json). That engine figure counts cash equivalents only, not marketable securities: the Q2 2026 release reports $838.9 million in cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities at June 30, 2026 (cited search result), so economic liquidity is materially stronger than the $141.2M net-debt line suggests. Liquidity is not the problem; cash generation is.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, first-mover real, economics unproven
Justification: First-to-market Rezdiffra with a patent estate extending to 2045, specialty pricing power (FY2024 gross margin 96.5% in fundamentals.json) and 49,000+ patients on therapy, but no demonstrated return on capital: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is negative in every recent year (-71.4% FY2023, -51.0% FY2024, -31.9% FY2025), conservative owner's earnings are negative in 0 of the last 5 years, revenue is a single product, and Wegovy's August 2025 MASH approval plus same-mechanism and FGF21 rivals end the monopoly. A 5 gives CAP 8.5 years.
- FOR: First FDA-approved MASH therapy (March 2024) for F2-F3 fibrosis — first-mover commercial infrastructure, physician familiarity and more than 49,000 patients on therapy at June 30, 2026; patent estate extending resmetirom protection — a new U.S. patent issued August 2025 extends protection to February 2045, plus three new patents issued in Q2 2026 including a compensated-cirrhosis (F4c) patent; specialty pricing power in the filed numbers: gross margin 96.5% in FY2024 (fundamentals.json) and Q2 2026 cost of sales of $40.0M on $364.3M of revenue in the company's release; once-daily oral, liver-directed THR-beta mechanism with no titration — a differentiated profile versus injectable GLP-1s in a large, under-diagnosed market (management: ~460,000 diagnosed patients).
- AGAINST: No demonstrated returns on capital: owner's earnings negative 0/5 of the last 5 years and roic_proxy negative in every recent year (-71.4% FY2023, -51.0% FY2024, -31.9% FY2025 in fundamentals.json); single-product concentration: 100% of revenue is Rezdiffra, pipeline beyond it unapproved and early; competition has arrived: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy was approved for the same F2-F3 MASH population in August 2025, Viking's VK2809 is a same-mechanism THR-beta rival, and FGF21 programs are now backed by Roche and Novo Nordisk; SBC is heavy and rising — $49.7M (FY2023) to $79.9M (FY2024) to $98.1M (FY2025) to $121.4M TTM — and the share count has compounded 9.4%/yr; payer pressure is building: management guided gross-to-net into the high-30% range for 2026 as payer agreements took effect.
- Gross-margin caveat: fundamentals.json captures a gross margin only for FY2024 (96.5%); the FY2025 and TTM gross-margin fields are null in that file, so no five-year margin trend is quoted — the Q2 2026 cost-of-sales figure from the company's own release (above) is the current-period evidence, and it points the same way (high specialty gross margin).
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection. (Moot for the score — see DCF.)

## DCF — Tier F: no scenario table exists, and that is the finding
The engine's Tier F branch fired: the base is not positive, so no scenarios, IVs, or IRRs are computed (implied_irr_weighted: null in dcf_numbers.json). Probabilities recorded for the run: 10/25/30/25/10 (defaults — nothing in the evidence justifies tilting weights for a branch that does not use them).
- **F sub-type: no_cash_generation** (f_subtype_basis: ttm.json legs, the TTM pin). On the TTM legs quoted above, operating cash flow itself is -$197,716,000 and capex is $8,569,000 — the business consumed cash from operations over the last twelve months, before the $121,429,000 of SBC is deducted. This is not an "SBC ate positive FCF" case on TTM: there is no positive FCF for SBC to eat.
- **Growth sanity check:** the engine's blend is 427.66% (key_numbers.md: rev CAGR 5y 432.66%, rev CAGR 3y 432.66%, latest rev YoY 432.05%). Every scenario start the engine could produce (base capped at 35%, super-bull start capped at 50%) sits far below the recent prints — FY2025 revenue $958,403,000 vs $180,133,000 in FY2024 (financials_history.csv), Q1 2026 net sales $311.3 million up 127% year over year and Q2 2026 net sales $364.3 million up 71% year over year, with trailing-twelve-month net sales of nearly $1.3 billion (company releases, cited search results). Written reason, as the spec requires: those prints are a launch ramp off a zero-revenue base (no revenue at all before FY2024), decelerating as the base normalizes (+127% in Q1 to +71% in Q2), not a steady-state growth rate — and decisively, growth applied to a negative base produces no valuation in any case. No growth input changes this tier.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved by construction — ttm.py was run, the base is the TTM figure through Q2 2026 quoted above, and the final engine run passed --ttm. The TTM base ($-11.27/share) is less negative than both the latest FY ($-12.84) and the 3-yr median ($-20.09), and still negative.
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 9.4%/yr; key_numbers.md share count CAGR 9.39%, growth adj -5.00%): real and already deducted via the growth adjustment. SBC trend checked in the filed history, and it is rising in dollars at every step: $49,735,000 (FY2023), $79,880,000 (FY2024), $98,130,000 (FY2025), $121,429,000 TTM (financials_history.csv / ttm.json). Diluted shares in the filed history rose from 18,687,774 (FY2023) to 22,434,310 (FY2025). This is a launch-stage company funding losses partly in stock; SBC is counted as a real cost throughout, which is a large part of why the OE base is negative.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump in the last 5 years): no divestiture, acquisition, or restatement — the break is the Rezdiffra commercial launch itself. Revenue was $0 in every filed year through FY2023, then $180,133,000 in FY2024 (FDA approval March 2024) and $958,403,000 in FY2025 (financials_history.csv). No CAGR in the blend is trusted as a run-rate; see the growth sanity check above.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025): resolved — the gap is non-cash stock compensation, not a tax deposit or impairment. FY2025 net income was -$288,284,000 against operating cash flow of -$189,553,000 (financials_history.csv), and the filed SBC addback for the same year is $98,130,000 with D&A of $1,506,000 — together they account for essentially the entire gap. That is also why FY2025 net income and conservative OE land at nearly the same figure (-$288,284,000 vs -$288,150,000): the OCF-based series adds SBC back only to deduct it again as a real cost. Separate one-off worth naming: Q3 2025 R&D included a $117 million one-time expense for the MGL-2086 global licensing agreement (CFO, Q3 2025 call, cited search result), and Q2 2026's net loss included a $25 million one-time business-development upfront (Q2 2026 call, cited search result) — recurring "one-time" licensing upfronts are this company's pipeline-building method, so no adjustment was made to the base for them; the tier is F with or without them.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (no diluted share count filed for 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019 — those history years use the basic / outstanding / dei count recorded in the shares_tag column): noted — per-share history for 2016–2019 is approximate. Immaterial to the verdict: those are pre-revenue years with deeply negative owner's earnings on any denominator, and they are outside the last-3-FY base window and the TTM legs.

## My thoughts / overlay
- There is no method range to hide behind here: TTM base -$11.27/share, latest-year-only -$12.84/share, 3-yr median -$20.09/share. Every defensible variant is Tier F. Anyone quoting a DCF value for MDGL today is projecting the inflection, not measuring owner's earnings.
- The inflection itself is real on the top line and is the bull case in full: nearly $1.3 billion of trailing-twelve-month net sales, more than 49,000 patients on therapy at June 30, 2026 (over 50,000 in early July), Q2 2026 sales up 71% year over year, a Germany launch, an expanded U.S. field force, three new resmetirom patents in Q2 2026, and a Phase 3 outcomes program in compensated cirrhosis (F4c) that would open a second, currently unapproved population (company releases and reporting, cited search results). None of that is owner's earnings yet: over the same twelve months the company burned $197,716,000 of operating cash and paid out $121,429,000 in stock compensation.
- The cost structure is the question, not demand.
